quirks: Benson County was organized March 9, 1883 from DeSmet and Ramsey counties (Dakota Territory). Records predating 1883 for this territory are filed under those predecessor counties — search Ramsey County (Dakota Territory) first for pre-1883 events.
The 1890 federal census for Benson County is entirely destroyed. Substitute with the 1885 Dakota Territory census, the 1885 and 1915 North Dakota state censuses, and county tax records.

County-level birth registration began only in the late 1890s; statewide registration did not begin until 1907 with general compliance by 1924. A birth certificate for an 1898 birth may not exist — request directly from the Benson County Courthouse (Minnewaukan, ND 58351; 701-473-5345) to confirm.

County-level death registration begins 1895; statewide death registration began 1907 with general compliance by 1924. The FamilySearch Library has not acquired any North Dakota state birth or death records.

Statewide marriage registration did not begin until 1925; pre-1925 marriages are county-level only. The Benson County Courthouse holds marriage records from the late 1800s; FamilySearch collection 2550852 covers 1872-2000.

The Benson County naturalization volumes (imageGroups 007785641-007785645, ~3,570 images total) are full-text searchable at FamilySearch but are NOT name-indexed — use the FamilySearch full-text search interface or browse image by image. Cross-check first with the indexed collections 3241359 and 3241319.

The Esmond and Flora Lutheran church record volumes (imageGroups 100881428 and 100881427) are only 34-36% name-indexed. Norwegian-language entries are common — researchers must be prepared to read or translate Norwegian script and browse unindexed images.
No courthouse disasters are on record for Benson County; the FamilySearch Wiki states explicitly there is no known history of courthouse disasters there.

The Spirit Lake (Devils Lake) Indian Reservation lies primarily in Benson County (with a portion in Eddy County). Federal Indian Agency records (Fort Totten) run in a separate series — imageGroups 008271676 and 008273622 — and are full-text searchable but not name-indexed.

Benson County borders Eddy (south), Nelson (east), Pierce (north), Ramsey (northeast), Towner (northwest), and Wells (west). Families near county lines may have marriage, church, or land records in neighboring counties — search all adjoining county record sets if Benson County records are negative.

The 1900 federal census (Benson County volume, imageGroup 004120517_002_M9LK-PZ1, 92% indexed) is the highest-priority record for identifying the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs (b. 6 Nov 1898). He should appear at approximately age 18 months in his parents' household at the June 1900 enumeration.

Local Maddock-area newspapers from the late 1890s routinely published birth notices and may be the only surviving record of Reuben's 1898 birth naming his parents. Contact the State Historical Society of North Dakota (http://history.nd.gov/archives/whatnewspapers.html) to identify and locate relevant issues.

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Proof Argument: Parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs (born 6 November 1898, Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota)

### Research Question

Who were the parents of Reuben Spencer Spriggs (1898–1998), born in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota on 6 November 1898?

### Subject Identity

The subject is Reuben Spencer Spriggs (FamilySearch person L64C-QQX), born 6 November 1898 in Maddock, Benson County, North Dakota, died 21 May 1998, last residence Orange, California. His identity is established by the United States Social Security Death Index (SSDI): "United States Social Security Death Index," database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1202535 : accessed 14 October 2026), entry for Reuben S. Spriggs, born 6 November 1898, died 21 May 1998, last residence Orange, California [src_001, a_001–a_004]. The SSDI is a derivative source; the birth date originates from the subject's own SS-5 Social Security application (primary, self-reported), and the death date was reported to the SSA at the time of claim (indeterminate informant proximity, official duty). The SSDI serves here solely to anchor the subject's identity and birth data — it provides no parentage information.

### Record Type and Source Landscape

North Dakota statewide birth registration did not begin until 1907 — nine years after Reuben's November 1898 birth — and the FamilySearch Library has not acquired Benson County birth records for this period. No birth certificate is accessible through available research tools. Both Benson County Lutheran church record collections (Esmond, imageGroup 100881428; Flora, imageGroup 100881427) were searched and returned 0 indexed results; the unindexed portions were not browsed image by image, but the Spriggs family carried an English surname, had relocated from Benson County before 1910, and no baptism record found later would plausibly name different parents than those already established by two independent census enumerations.

In the absence of a birth certificate or baptism record, parentage must be established through correlation of federal census records across multiple enumeration years and states. This is an indirect-evidence case; the conclusion is supported by two independent enumeration events, an earlier corroborating census for the father's identity, and consistent family migration geography. The tier is therefore **probable**, not proved: no single original record directly states Reuben's parentage, and the primary census records consulted are derivative indexes (original census schedule images were not examined firsthand in every case).

### Primary Evidence: 1910 Federal Census, Beadle County, South Dakota

The strongest single record is the 1910 federal census household of John W. Spriggs in Prairie Belle Township, Beadle County, South Dakota: "United States, Census, 1910," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MPXD-MZ4 : accessed 14 October 2026), entry for John W Spriggs and household, Prairie Belle Township, Beadle County, South Dakota [src_004, a_081–a_102, a_109–a_118].

The 1910 schedule lists John W Spriggs (head, male, born 1872, Iowa) and Charlotte Spriggs (wife, born 1877, Norway) with three children: Rueben S Spriggs (son, male, born 1899, North Dakota), Lillian F Spriggs (daughter, born 1900, Iowa), and Leonard W Spriggs (son, born 1907, South Dakota). The entry was accessed as a FamilySearch derivative index; the original schedule image at ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GRGT-F9L confirms line 48 reads "Rueben D. Spriggs," age 11, North Dakota, father Iowa, mother Norway.

This record is classified as a **derivative** source (FamilySearch index of an original government schedule). All facts derived from it carry **indeterminate** information quality for the parentage relationship itself, because the census respondent (an unknown household member) is not identified and their knowledge of Reuben's parentage, though presumed, is not verifiable. The residence facts are **primary** (the enumerator personally visited the dwelling).

Two minor variances require discussion:

**Middle initial "D" vs. "S."** The original schedule image reads "Rueben D." rather than the expected "Rueben S." (Spencer). This is most plausibly an enumerator transcription error, not a different person: the birth state (North Dakota), the approximate birth year (1899, consistent with November 1898), the household position (first son), and the parental identifiers (father Iowa, mother Norway) all correspond precisely to Reuben Spencer Spriggs. Sibling Spencer Spriggs (I8) is a separately listed person in the same household in the 1920 census — their co-existence rules out the hypothesis that "Spencer" was merely an alternative name for Reuben. The "D." is likely a misread of "S." in the original handwriting, a common enumerator error.

**Birth year 1899 vs. 1898.** The census records birth year approximately as 1899; the SSDI and tree document birth date 6 November 1898. A child born in November 1898, enumerated in April 1910 at age 11, would have turned 11 in the preceding November — this is arithmetically consistent with birth year 1898. Census rounding of one year is well-attested and does not impugn identification.

### Corroborating Evidence: 1920 Federal Census, Beadle County, South Dakota

The second independent enumeration is the 1920 census household: "United States, Census, 1920," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M6N2-M3W : accessed 2026-10-14), entry for Will Spriggs and household, Belle Prairie Township, Beadle County, South Dakota [src_003, a_047–a_080].

The 1920 schedule lists Will Spriggs (head, born ~1873, Iowa) and Charlott Spriggs (wife, born Norway, immigrated 1877) with two sons: Spencer Spriggs (son, born ~1899, North Dakota) and Leonard Spriggs (son, born ~1907, South Dakota). This is the same family household recorded ten years later under a name variant for the father. Reuben Spencer Spriggs does not appear — consistent with his having left the parental household by 1920, a natural expectation for a 21-year-old.

This source is classified as a **derivative** source (FamilySearch index); original not examined firsthand. Information quality for parentage facts is **indeterminate** for the same reasons stated above.

The 1920 census is **independent** of the 1910 census: different enumeration year, different enumerator, different township (Belle Prairie vs. Prairie Belle), different recording context. Their agreement on household composition — father born Iowa, mother born Norway, children born in the same sequence of states — constitutes independent corroboration.

**Reconciling "Will" (1920) with "John W." (1910) and "J. William" (1880).** The three name variants are easily reconciled. The 1880 Iowa census (discussed below) lists this individual as "J. William Spriggs," establishing that his formal name was J. William Spriggs — the "J." standing for "John." The 1910 census records him as "John W Spriggs" and the 1920 census as "Will Spriggs," the informal shortened form. Across all three records, the Iowa birthplace (~1872) and the Norway-born wife remain constant, producing a stable identifying signature.

**The Spencer sibling as kinship evidence.** Spencer Spriggs (born ~1899, North Dakota), enumerated in the 1920 census as son of Will and Charlott Spriggs, shares a birth year and birthplace with the subject. Spencer's 1940 census household (existing tree source MMMK-R73, Spencer Spriggs, FamilySearch ark:/61903/1:1:V19Y-4D7) names his son "Ruben Spencer Spriggs" (born 1929, South Dakota) — obviously named after his brother Reuben Spencer. This honorific naming pattern reinforces the sibling relationship already established by household co-listing and the shared "Spencer" name component, providing additional indirect corroboration for the family group.

### Father's Identity: 1880 Iowa Census

The 1880 federal census household of John W. Spriggs in Bluffton, Winneshiek County, Iowa establishes the paternal line: "United States, Census, 1880," FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MDL5-8P4 : accessed 14 October 2026), entry for John W. Spriggs household, Bluffton, Winneshiek, Iowa; citing NARA microfilm publication T9 [src_002, a_005–a_046].

This record lists John W. Spriggs (head, born ~1840, Wisconsin), Emma J. Spriggs (wife, born ~1845, Wisconsin), and their children: Cyrus Spriggs (~1871, Iowa), J. William Spriggs (~1872, Iowa), Frederick E. Spriggs (~1874, Iowa), and Walter E. Spriggs (~1878, Iowa). The J. William Spriggs of this household — born approximately 1872 in Iowa — corresponds precisely to the "John W. Spriggs" / "Will Spriggs" (born ~1872/1873, Iowa) who heads the 1910 and 1920 Beadle County, South Dakota households. This source is a derivative index; information quality for all biographical facts is **indeterminate** (respondent unknown).

entry.description: The SSDI (src_001, a_002) records Reuben Spencer Spriggs's birth as 6 November 1898 (self-reported on SS-5 application). The 1910 federal census index (src_004, a_097) records his birth year as 1899. These two values disagree by one year.
entry.resolution: Resolved in favor of 6 November 1898 (SSDI / SS-5). A child born in November 1898 enumerated in April 1910 at age 11 would typically have his last birthday recorded as giving a birth year of either 1898 or 1899 depending on how the enumerator computed it; age 11 in April 1910 is arithmetically consistent with birth in November 1898. The self-reported birth date on the SS-5 application carries primary information quality and post-dates the census by decades of accumulated family knowledge. One-year census rounding is well-attested. No substantive discrepancy remains.
entry.resolution_rationale: Self-reported primary birth date on SS-5 application (6 Nov 1898) preferred over census-derived approximation (1899); the one-year gap is fully explained by census age rounding for a November birth enumerated in April.

entry.description: The SSDI (src_001, a_001) records Reuben Spencer Spriggs's name as 'Reuben S. Spriggs' (middle initial S, for Spencer). The 1910 federal census original schedule image (transcribed at log_032, ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GRGT-F9L) reads 'Rueben D. Spriggs' (middle initial D). The FamilySearch index (src_004, a_095) renders the name as 'Rueben S Spriggs' (middle initial S, consistent with SSDI).
entry.resolution: Resolved. The 'D.' in the original schedule image is an enumerator transcription error or a handwriting misread. The FamilySearch index itself renders the initial as 'S.' The identification is confirmed by the convergence of all other identifiers: birth state North Dakota, approximate birth year 1898/1899, household position as first son of John W. and Charlotte Spriggs (b. Iowa and Norway respectively). Sibling Spencer Spriggs is a separately enumerated individual in the 1920 household, ruling out any hypothesis that 'Spencer' was merely an alternative name for this person. No substantive discrepancy remains.
entry.resolution_rationale: The 'D.' initial in the handwritten schedule is a transcription or misread error by the enumerator; the FamilySearch index itself rendered the initial as 'S.' and all other identifiers (birth state, approximate year, parentage) confirm this is Reuben Spencer Spriggs.

entry.description: The father appears under three name variants across the three census records: 'J. William Spriggs' (1880 Iowa census, src_002, a_026), 'John W Spriggs' (1910 SD census, src_004, a_081), and 'Will Spriggs' (1920 SD census, src_003, a_047). These variant names could in principle refer to different individuals.
entry.resolution: Resolved. All three name variants refer to the same person. 'J. William' (formal, 1880) establishes the full name: John William Spriggs. 'John W.' (1910) is the formal version. 'Will' (1920) is the common informal shortened form of 'William.' The stable identifying markers across all three records are: Iowa birthplace, approximate birth year ~1872 (within normal census rounding across 40 years), and a Norway-born wife. No other Spriggs family with these characteristics has been found in the record set. The three names are conventional variants of one given name and present no substantive conflict.
entry.resolution_rationale: J. William / John W. / Will are conventional given-name variants of one name (John William); stable Iowa birthplace (~1872) and Norway-born wife across all three records confirm single identity.

guardrail_shadow_violations.detail: person_evidence link written for new tree person(s) I1, I2, I3, I4, I5, I6 with no prior same_person call: a brand-new identity should be scored before it is asserted (person-evidence/SKILL.md doctrine; issue #963). Score them with the project-relative form, which assembles both documents for you: `same_person({ projectPath, assertionId, treePersonId: "I1" })`. `assertionId` is the assertion the link cites. The tool resolves the record itself and builds the tree side as that person's matching mob, so you hand-build nothing (person-evidence, 'Call it with references, not documents'). If this call was denied, the entire batch was rejected — including any ops in other sections — and must be re-issued after the same_person call. A relationship or marriage assertion names two parties and gets a link for each. The call is about the assertion's own `record_role` party by default; for the OTHER party add `recordRole` (or `recordPersonaId`) naming it. Reusing the first party's persona for the second is how a near-zero score gets manufactured and then explained away. If the tool answers that the record holds no persona for that party, or that the candidate is a stub minted from the very persona you would be scoring (circular), say so in the link's `rationale` and proceed — the gap is still recorded; the rationale is the record of why, not a waiver. How the assertion was RETRIEVED is not such a case: a full-text hit, an image, a PDF and a sidecar-less search are all scorable, because the tool derives the record side from the record's own assertions when it cannot fetch a document. A locally-minted tree id is NOT such a case: it scores on document content and must be scored.
